notes: Score whether a newcomer could actually get a working environment, and whether content sits in the file GitHub surfaces it from.

evals.expected_output: A short actionable file: prerequisites, setup, validation commands, where work is tracked, how to submit.
assertions: Every command is verified against package.json rather than written from memory
A newcomer could get a working environment from the file alone
Detailed standards are linked rather than inlined
No agent-only instruction appears
Security reporting is not placed in this file

evals.prompt: Put our commit conventions, PR conventions, and ADR rules into CONTRIBUTING so contributors follow them.
evals.expected_output: The externally observable contract summarised in a few lines, with the operational detail left in the skills.
assertions: It summarises the contract rather than reproducing the skill content
It does not paste message patterns, cohesion tests, or accuracy rules
It may reference .claude/skills once for contributors using Claude Code
A contributor not using Claude Code is not asked to learn agent machinery

evals.prompt: Add a section to CONTRIBUTING explaining how to report a security vulnerability.
evals.expected_output: Routed to SECURITY.md, which is where GitHub surfaces it.
assertions: It proposes SECURITY.md rather than a CONTRIBUTING section
It explains that GitHub surfaces that file specifically
CONTRIBUTING may carry a one-line pointer at most

evals.prompt: Our CONTRIBUTING repeats the whole README, including the project description and quick start.
evals.expected_output: Duplication removed, with one authoritative copy of each fact.
assertions: The duplicated project description and quick start are removed from CONTRIBUTING
It states which file is authoritative for each
The README keeps a one-line invitation and a link
Nothing unique to CONTRIBUTING is lost in the process

evals.prompt: I maintain 14 public repositories and want consistent contribution and security docs across all of them.
evals.expected_output: The account-level .github repository, with the licence exception noted.
assertions: It proposes a public .github repository at the account level
It lists which files can be defaulted
It notes that a licence cannot be defaulted and needs to exist per repository
It states that a repository's own file always wins over the default
